tasks.title: An image with alt
tasks.statement: There is no photo under the paragraph. Add a picture of the office: the file `office.jpg`, with a text alternative that conveys the meaning of the photo (for example, “Office building on the main street”).
tasks.hint: The `img` tag is empty and has no closing tag. You need two attributes: `src` with the address and `alt` describing what is in the photo.

tasks.title: A decorative image
tasks.statement: The wavy line `wave.svg` only decorates the heading and conveys nothing. Make a screen reader skip it, but keep the text-alternative attribute in the markup.
tasks.hint: An empty string is a value: `alt=""`. If you remove the attribute entirely, the screen reader will read out the file name.

tasks.title: An image link
tasks.statement: The bag icon leads to the cart. Right now the image has no alternative, so a screen reader cannot tell where the link goes. Write an `alt` that describes the action, containing the word “cart”.
tasks.hint: For a link, `alt` says not “bag” but what happens on click: “Open the cart”.

tasks.title: Dimensions against layout jumps
tasks.statement: The hero image `hero.jpg` is 800 by 450 pixels. Tell the browser the dimensions in the markup so that it reserves space before the file loads.
tasks.hint: The attributes are `width` and `height`; the values are plain numbers without units.

tasks.title: An illustration with a caption
tasks.statement: Wrap the picture `chart.png` in a self-contained block and add the caption “Fig. 1. Revenue by quarter”. The caption must come after the picture.
tasks.hint: You need the pair `figure` and `figcaption`; `img` goes inside `figure`, and so does `figcaption`, after the picture.

tasks.title: picture with formats
tasks.statement: Attach three files of the same image: `cat.avif`, `cat.webp` and the fallback `cat.jpg`. The modern formats come first and differ by the `type` attribute; the fallback is a regular `img` with `alt`.
tasks.hint: Inside `picture`, first two `source` elements (`type="image/avif"`, `type="image/webp"`, addresses in `srcset`), and the `img` last.

tasks.title: srcset and sizes
tasks.statement: The hero image has three files: `hero-400.jpg` (400 px), `hero-800.jpg` (800 px), `hero-1600.jpg` (1600 px). List them in `srcset` with widths in `w` descriptors, and in `sizes` say: on windows wider than 900px the image takes a third of the width, on narrow ones the full width.
tasks.hint: `srcset="a.jpg 400w, b.jpg 800w"`; `sizes="(min-width: 900px) 33vw, 100vw"`. Keep `src` and `alt`: old browsers and the screen reader need them.

tasks.title: Lazy and eager
tasks.statement: On the page the main image `#hero` is visible immediately, while `#g1` and `#g2` sit in a gallery below the first screen. Turn on lazy loading for the gallery, and give the main image a high priority without making it lazy.
tasks.hint: For the gallery: `loading="lazy"`. For the main image: `fetchpriority="high"`, and it must not have a `loading` attribute.

tasks.title: Video with subtitles
tasks.statement: Build a player: controls, the poster `poster.jpg`, two files (`intro.webm` with type `video/webm` and `intro.mp4` with type `video/mp4`), Russian subtitles `ru.vtt`, and fallback text for browsers that do not support video, placed inside the tag. Write the fallback text with the word “browser” in it.
tasks.hint: Inside `video`: two `source` elements, one `track` with `kind="subtitles"` and `srclang="ru"`, and then plain text. `controls` is written without a value.

tasks.title: A podcast on the page
tasks.statement: Under the heading, add a podcast player: controls and two formats, `episode.mp3` (`audio/mpeg`) and `episode.ogg` (`audio/ogg`). For old browsers, put a download link inside the tag.
tasks.hint: `audio` with the `controls` attribute; inside, two `source` elements and an `a` link with `href`.

tasks.title: A safe map
tasks.statement: The map is embedded in a frame with no preparation. Give the frame a name for screen readers (“Office map”), forbid it everything unnecessary through `sandbox` (the map's scripts may run, but top-window navigation must not be allowed), and defer loading until the frame is near the screen.
tasks.hint: The attributes are `title`, `sandbox="allow-scripts"`, `loading="lazy"`. Values like `allow-top-navigation…` are not needed.

tasks.title: A table with a header
tasks.statement: The price list is written as bare rows. Give the table the caption “Price list” (`caption`), move the first row into the header (`thead`) and make its cells headings (`th`); the data rows go in `tbody`.
tasks.hint: Order inside `table`: `caption`, `thead`, `tbody`. In the header the cells are `th`, in the data they are `td`.

tasks.title: Headings with scope
tasks.statement: In the weather table the headings are not tied to the data. Declare the column headings (`scope="col"`), and turn the city names in the rows into `th` heading cells with `scope="row"`. Leave the empty corner cell alone.
tasks.hint: In `thead`, give every `th` `scope="col"`. In `tbody`, the first cell of each row is not a `td` but a `th scope="row"`.

tasks.title: A two-level header
tasks.statement: Make the header out of two rows: the cell “City” spans both rows (`rowspan`), and above “January” and “July” there is a shared cell “Temperature” (`colspan`). The second header row keeps only “January” and “July”.
tasks.hint: First row: `th rowspan="2"` with “City” and `th colspan="2"` with “Temperature”. Second row: two `th`. `scope="colgroup"` suits the cell merged across columns.

tasks.title: A collapsible answer
tasks.statement: The question and the answer sit in ordinary blocks. Collapse the answer into the ready-made widget: the question is a heading that is always visible, and the answer is shown on click.
tasks.hint: `details` contains a `summary` (as the first child) with the question text, and then a paragraph with the answer.

tasks.title: A gallery with captions
tasks.statement: Three photos sit in one block with no captions. Build a gallery: a bulleted list of three items, each holding a `figure` with a picture and a caption (`figcaption`: “Lake”, “Forest”, “Mountains”).
tasks.hint: `ul` > `li` > `figure` > `img` and `figcaption`. Do not forget to keep the `alt` on every picture.

tasks.title: No table for layout
tasks.statement: A page with a menu on the left and text on the right is laid out with a table: that was common long ago, but a table is for data. Rewrite the markup semantically: the menu is a `nav` with two links, the main text is `main`. There must be no tables.
tasks.hint: Remove `table`, `tr` and `td`. Columns are arranged later by CSS (flex or grid); for the markup, `nav` and `main` in the right order are enough.

tasks.title: An icon in the markup
tasks.statement: A round icon is inserted straight into the page, but a screen reader does not know what it is. Make it a picture named “Information”: the `img` role and a nested `title`.
tasks.hint: On `svg`, write `role="img"`, and put `<title>Information</title>` as the first child.
